ideas.description:
Exploit: run one more screen of time cuts, then launch once (the I124 protocol) on the new I125 base. Base: drafts/I125_base.py, which is the E082 tip plus the compiled lookahead blend plus the whole-epoch low-res resize. That base is bit-identical to E082 in unit tests and saves ~0.032 s/trial. Run ONE process with one build on seeds 3-42 (40 seeds), with configs alternating per seed so they share autotuned kernels. Configs:
- c0 = I125 base as is.
- c1 = c0 + block-1 freeze at 0.75 of total samples (sample 257813 of 343750 instead of 275000). This is E079's priced cut: -0.05 pp paired for -0.9%.
- c2 = c0 + a 25 px middle stage (samples 75000-175000 at 25 px; sizes 24/12/6/3, final map 3x3, static-kernel max_pool2d(3)). This is I113's narrow miss: -0.105 pp for -1.8%.
- c3 = c0 + both cuts.
Also fold into c1-c3 (never into c0) any arm promoted by the prepare-overhead gate, the I129 projection gate, the NS-overlap gate or the explore screens below, if they pass first. Warm every new partial shape (257813, 75000/175000 at 25 px, run end) in build() with channels_last tensors (E035), and run debug_nan.py.
Launch rule, pre-registered and corrected for process offset:
- m = 40-seed mean.
- t = offline prepare+train × (E082 harness 4.584 s / E082-config offline time from the I124 log).
- P = Φ((m − 0.7530)/0.19). The sd 0.19 combines the 3-seed sd of 0.16, the build/process offset of ~0.10 (I123) and the estimation SE of 0.05.
- EV = P × (4.584 − t).
Launch the argmax-EV config once on seeds 0-2 only if P ≥ 0.60 and t ≤ 4.55 s. Never re-roll. Report seeds 33-42 separately as fresh seeds.
ideas.expected: c0: m ~0.7541, t ~4.55 s (P ~0.72, EV ~0.024). c1: m ~0.7536, t ~4.51 s (P ~0.62, EV ~0.045). c2: m ~0.7531, t ~4.47 s (P ~0.52, fails the P rule). c3: m ~0.7526 (fails). The most likely launch is c1, giving a new tip at ~4.50-4.52 s (-1.5% vs 4.584) with ~60% chance of clearing 0.753. If no config meets the rule, launch nothing: the frontier is flat at ~0.05 pp per 1% of time, so every non-math-preserving cut has to be paid for with a real accuracy gain first.

ideas.description: Systems, math-preserving: remove the remaining trial-0 prepare excess. I122 measured prepare at 0.095 s on trial 0 and 0.017 s afterwards, even with the E077 warmups, which is ~0.026 s/trial on average (~0.6%). Gate in drafts/ on the I125 base: in a fresh process, time each prepare() component over 3 consecutive trials with cuda-synchronized timers. Components: file open/read/unpickle, numpy→torch conversion, pinned staging copy, H2D, label conversion, whitening covariance and eigh, parameter/buffer/optimizer/lookahead/Muon resets, generator seeding, first randperm on the trial generator. Find which component carries the trial-0 excess. If it can be warmed legally in build() on synthetic inputs, do that and nothing else. Examples: first use of torch.Generator on CUDA, eigh at a new dtype or shape, first foreach zero_/copy_ over the parameter lists, first unpickle code path on a synthetic in-memory pickle of the same structure. Never read the real data file in build(). Require same-process per-seed equality with the I125 base on seeds 0-2. Do not launch alone; fold it into the stack screen's c1-c3 if it passes. If the excess comes from the first real file read (page cache), record that prepare is at its legal floor and retire.
ideas.expected: About 55% chance the excess can be warmed legally. If so, mean prepare falls from ~0.043 s to ~0.017 s, so time drops by ~0.02-0.03 s/trial (-0.4% to -0.6%) with accuracy math unchanged. Otherwise there is no run, and the outside-step axis is fully closed.

ideas.description: Explore. This proposes a new node, H1.7.5: the SGD group's weight-decay STRENGTH is off its optimum. Every SGD-group test so far (E039, E045, E049, E056, E072) held lr×wd constant, so the wd level inherited from CIFAR-10 airbench (0.012 × multipliers) was never varied on its own. Under Muon with weight-norm projection, wd acts only on the 100×576 head and the BN biases (plus the whitening bias in epoch 1). Head wd sets how fast row norms, and therefore logit sharpness, grow. With 100 classes and ~215 steps, that may be badly tuned. Base: I125 base. Run two arms in ONE process on seeds 3-22, paired against the base in the same process: (a) every SGD-group wd ×0.5; (b) every SGD-group wd ×2. The lrs stay unchanged. wd is an eager torch-SGD param-group value, so nothing recompiles and the screen's times are valid. Promote an arm into the stack screen only if its paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.2%). Paired delta per arm -0.3 to +0.25 pp, point -0.02 pp for ×2 and +0.04 pp for ×0.5 (a short horizon tends to want less regularization, but LS was flat). A gain ≥ +0.12 pp at 2 SE is a free buffer worth ~2.5% of time at the frontier rate. Both arms within 1 SE closes the SGD group entirely (lr, head, BN and wd).

ideas.description: Explore. This proposes a new node, H1.15: class-stratified batches lower the head's gradient noise in a 100-class, ~215-step run. At bs 1536 a random batch holds 15.4 ± ~3.9 samples per class, so some classes get almost no head gradient on a given step. Muon normalizes the filters' updates away from that noise, but the SGD head and BN biases do not. Change only how the per-epoch permutation is built: for each epoch, draw one random permutation per class from the trial generator, take each sample's rank r within its class (CIFAR-100 has exactly 500 per class), set key = (r + U(0,1))/500, and use argsort(key) as the epoch order. Every window of 1536 then holds ~15-16 samples of each class, while the within-class order stays random. Implement it vectorised on the GPU inside the fused augment's permutation step (rank via a sort of class-major keys), with no Python loop over classes. All RNG comes from the trial generator in prepare/train. Augment draws and stage boundaries are unchanged. Warm the new permutation code in build() on synthetic labels. Screen in ONE process on seeds 3-22, paired against the I125 base. Promote only if the paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE and offline time is within +0.3%.
ideas.expected: Time +0.0% to +0.3% (one extra argsort of 50k keys per epoch). Paired delta -0.15 to +0.25 pp, point +0.05 pp. A gain ≥ +0.12 pp at 2 SE supports H1.15 and is a free buffer for the stack. Within ±1 SE: per-step class coverage is not limiting at bs 1536, so close it.

ideas.description: Systems explore. This proposes a new node, H2.6: Muon's NS GEMMs (~1.13 ms/step, ~5% of the trial) can be hidden behind backward instead of removed. Today the whole forward+backward is one compiled graph, so no gradient is available before backward ends. Gate in drafts/ before writing any submission code: microbenchmark on the A100, with real shapes at bs 1536 and 32 px. Launch the block-3 576×5184 NS group (PE-NS3, compiled) on a side CUDA stream concurrently with the compiled backward of blocks 1-2. Measure the combined wall time against the sum of the two run serially. Continue only if the measured overlap saving is ≥ 0.35 ms/step. If so, make one change: split the compiled model into two regions, (blocks 1-2) and (block 3 + head), with one intentional graph break, so region 2's backward finishes first. When block 3's grads are ready, launch block 3's Muon update (momentum, PE-NS3, rescale, projection) on a side stream with proper event waits. Join before the next forward and before the lookahead sync. Blocks 1-2 keep the existing batched Muon step, in both freeze variants. The math is identical op for op. Warm every region and variant in build(), and check same-process per-seed equality with the base on seeds 0-2. Do not launch alone; fold into the stack screen if the offline time saving is ≥ 0.8%.
ideas.expected: About 65% chance the gate fails, because the 31×31/15×15 backward convs at bs 1536 already fill the SMs; then retire H2.6 with no run. If it passes: Muon cost hidden 0.3-0.5 ms/step, time -0.8% to -1.8%, point -1.2%, with accuracy math unchanged (it still re-draws across processes like any build change).

ideas.description: Explore the last untuned SGD-group scalar: its Nesterov momentum, inherited from airbench (0.85). Muon momentum turned out to have a sharp optimum (I126: 0.9 cost -0.52 pp, 0.7 cost -0.20 pp), so a mis-set head/BN momentum could matter as much, and it was never varied. Base: I125 base. Run two arms in ONE process on seeds 3-22, paired against the base in the same process: SGD-group momentum 0.8 and 0.9, with lr and wd unchanged. Torch SGD's effective step scales with 1/(1−μ), so the arms also change the effective lr; report that confound in the log. The value is an eager param-group setting, so nothing recompiles. Promote an arm only if its paired gain is ≥ +0.12 pp at ≥ 2 SE.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. Paired delta per arm -0.35 to +0.15 pp, point -0.05 pp (airbench tuned 0.85 jointly with this lr). Both arms within 1 SE closes every SGD-group knob. A drop ≥ 0.2 pp on one side confirms that 0.85 is a sharp optimum, as Muon's 0.8 is.

The queue now holds 7 ideas: I129 (projection-frequency gate, still running) and 6 new ones.

**Why the next step looks like this.** E082 is the tip at 4.584 s. Its one-process 30-seed mean (~0.7541) is only ~0.1 pp above the gate. Every lever that was priced but changes the training math sits on a flat frontier of ~0.05 pp per 1% of time:
- block-1 freeze at 0.75
- 25 px middle stage
- extra epochs

So the only real gains left are math-preserving time cuts or a genuine accuracy gain.

**Exploit ideas:**
- **Priority 5: launch-once stack screen on the I125 base.** I125 is a math-preserving cut worth -0.7%. The screen runs on 40 seeds in one process with four configs: base, freeze at 0.75, 25 px, and both. The launch probability now also counts the ~0.1 pp build/process offset from I123. Expected result: a launch of the freeze-0.75 config at ~4.51 s with about a 60% chance of clearing the gate.
- **Priority 4: the remaining trial-0 prepare excess.** Worth ~0.6%, and it can only be cut if a legal synthetic warmup exists.
- **Priority 2: hide block-3 Muon NS behind the block-1/2 backward on a side stream.** This is a new mechanism (proposed H2.6). It sits behind a strict microbenchmark gate.

**Explore ideas (untested scalars and mechanisms, all screened in one process for a paired gain of ≥ 2 SE):**
- SGD-group weight-decay strength at fixed lr. Every earlier test held lr×wd constant, so the wd level itself was never varied.
- Class-stratified batches to cut the 100-way head's gradient noise (proposed H1.15).
- SGD-group Nesterov momentum. Muon's momentum turned out to have a sharp optimum, so this one may too.

**No drops.** Every other queued idea is already done or dropped.

**Tree bookkeeping the hypothesis owner should do** (results already settle these):
- Close H1.2.9 (I098), H1.6/H1.6.1 (I104, I108), H1.12.1 (I105), H1.13.1 (I120), H1.1.5 (residual present), H1.14.1 (I123) and H2.5.1 (I117 refuted).
- Mark H4.1.8 supported: paired sd is ~0.3-0.4 pp.
